## The project

The **Stablecoin Opportunity Map** asks where alternative payment infrastructure — specifically dollar-denominated stablecoins on public blockchain rails — would unlock the most economically valuable trade.

The premise is that complex products (semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, machinery) depend on a fragile bank-to-bank chain of trust to clear payment, and that this chain has been quietly breaking under post-2014 de-risking pressure. If stablecoins bypass the chain, the marginal value of adoption should be highest where the chain is most strained *and* the underlying trade is most complex. This site lets you see the framework applied country-by-country.

## Acknowledgments

The full analysis pipeline, manuscript drafting, and this companion site were built in **Claude Code** with the author providing the research questions, theoretical scaffolding, and review at every stage. All errors are the author's.

The economic-complexity tooling builds on the Harvard Growth Lab's *Atlas of Economic Complexity* and the methodology of Hidalgo & Hausmann (2009). The de-risking framing draws on the BIS *Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures* literature and on World Bank correspondent-banking surveys.

## Companion site

- This site is generated by [Quarto](https://quarto.org) with [Observable JS](https://observablehq.com) reactive blocks. Source: `site/` in the project repository.
- Charts use [Observable Plot](https://observablehq.com/plot) and [D3.js](https://d3js.org); typography is Source Serif Pro.
- Hosting: GitHub Pages, served from the `docs/` folder of the main branch.

## How to cite

Until a permanent venue is announced, please cite the working-paper PDF:

> Prudencio, D. (2026). *The Stablecoin Opportunity Map: Economic Complexity Meets Payment Innovation*. Working paper.
